title: SongForge Capacity Thesis
description: Issue #18 AC4: the shape proof for PRD #6 / decision #8 -- sse_connected_listeners rises with the number of connected clients while radio_advances_total and datastore-op counters stay flat, because SSE fan-out is in-process off ONE Redis pub/sub subscription per app instance. Also charts write-path throughput (AC4b). MULTI-INSTANCE: Prometheus discovers every `web` replica via DNS, so per-PROCESS metrics (listeners, created, relayed) are sum()'d for the fleet total AND broken out per instance, while DB-DERIVED gauges (jobs_in_state) -- which every instance sets to the same global count -- use max() to avoid double-counting.

panels.title: Connected listeners + fan-out (both EXPECTED TO RISE)
panels.description: songforge_sse_connected_listeners is a PER-PROCESS gauge, so the fleet total is sum() across instances (connection-ceiling.js drives this up); the per-instance series ({{instance}}) show how the load balancer spreads connections and where each instance hits its own ceiling. The relayed-events rate is the in-process fan-out work (once per listener per push), also summed across instances -- it belongs on the 'rises' side. The thesis is these climb while the datastore panels below stay flat.

panels.title: Radio advance + pointer PUBLISH rate (expected FLAT)
panels.description: sum(rate(songforge_radio_advances_total[1m])) and sum(rate(songforge_radio_pointer_events_published_total[1m])) -- the thesis's direct observable: these stay flat regardless of listener count, because only ONE leader drives the clock-triggered advance and publishes each pointer change ONCE to Redis. Summed across instances so the single leader's rate shows regardless of which replica currently holds the lease (non-leaders contribute 0). (The per-listener relay counter is deliberately NOT here -- it grows with listeners and lives on the 'rises' panel to the left.)

panels.title: Datastore-op rate (expected FLAT as listener count rises)
panels.description: ACTUAL datastore operations from the exporters -- Postgres transactions (pg_stat_database_xact_commit + xact_rollback) and Redis commands (redis_commands_processed_total). These, not HTTP request volume, are the datastore-facing work that must NOT scale with sse_connected_listeners: a listener holds an in-process SSE connection and never issues a per-tick datastore read/write. (HTTP request rate would rise here just from new /events connections + /metrics scrapes, so it can't establish datastore-independence -- it lives on the Service RED dashboard instead.) Scraped from the single exporter per datastore, so unaffected by web replica count.

panels.title: Write-path throughput + backlog (AC4b)
panels.description: jobs_dispatched_total is incremented in the WORKER process, which runs no HTTP server and is NOT scraped by Prometheus -- so it is unobservable here and this panel does NOT use it. Instead: sum(rate(songforge_jobs_created_total[1m])) is the create rate (per-process web counter, summed across replicas), and the DB-derived songforge_jobs_in_state gauge (set by the web process from a live GROUP BY state, so max() across replicas = the one true global count) shows the pipeline draining. If the write path keeps pace, the QUEUED backlog stays flat/low and in-flight sits near the global generation cap; if dispatch falls behind (e.g. GLOBAL_GENERATION_CONCURRENCY too low), QUEUED climbs without bound -- the exact signal observed at cap=1 (backlog grew to thousands) vs cap=50 (backlog drained). Backlog/in-flight are counts on the right axis; create rate is req/s on the left.
